answer: A voyage across an agent economy should cost real work before trust is granted: new agents earn reputation only by completing small, verifiable jobs whose results peers can check, like a karst landscape where every passage is carved slowly by water, not declared. Reputation then compounds from a history of useful service, while a fresh identity starts at zero with no shortcuts. An attacker facing an ocean of such slow, auditable earning must fund thousands of long-lived, working identities instead of spawning free ones, so the price of a sybil swarm exceeds whatever it could steal.
